market_holds: Spot $3.91 at the 2026-11-23 seal, -64.8% from the 52w high and 10% above the low (sealed baseline). The 52w high was hit before the CSRC action of 2026-05-22, which put mainland clients on sell-only and fined the company; the stock fell about 25-31% that day. Options: event-implied move 5.62% (7.8% front straddle net of ordinary vol), 25d skew +3.4 vol pts to puts, put/call OI 0.22, ATM spread 29% of mid (baseline). Run-in: -3.0% over 5d and -4.4% over 20d. Day to day, TIGR moves tick for tick with FUTU: 11-17 -6.2/-5.1, 11-18 -6.1/-4.3, 11-19 +7.3/+4.8, 11-20 -3.7/-4.8, 11-23 +7.1/+6.9 (Yahoo bars). The tape is extraordinarily volatile, QQQ -5.7% on 11-20 and +7.1% on 11-23, so ordinary overnight-plus-morning noise is on the order of the implied event move. Consensus: non-GAAP EPS $0.21 for Q3 (Benzinga, updated 2026-10-30, before Futu's print). Chartmill shows $0.28 EPS and $177.25M revenue (undated, said to be revised up about 20% over 3 months); I treat that figure as uncertain. Guide context from the Q2 call (2026-08-26): Q3-to-date volume and commissions 'slightly below Q2'; new funded accounts flat or higher than Q2's 32.6k; client assets up high single digits QTD; mainland outflows 'largely run their course'; $50M buyback with about $5M done. Futu's Q3 print (2026-11-19) is the closest read-through and is already in the price: TIGR rose 7.3% that day while QQQ fell 2.2%.
view: This quarter is a step down from a record Q2, and the peer has already shown roughly how big the step is. Futu said in August that its Q3-to-date volume was down 'modestly' and finished the quarter at -22% QoQ: US -24%, HK -19%, commissions -17%, margin balances -22%. Its interest and other income were flat to up (+1.6% QoQ by my back-calculation), and revenue fell 7.1% QoQ. Tiger said almost the same thing in August ('slightly below Q2'), so its Q3 commissions are probably down 15-20% from Q2's $78.3M. Interest income ($83M) is probably flat, and other/IPO income (~$21M) is held up by a record HK Q3 for share sales. That gives revenue of roughly $165-172M against Q2's $182.3M (own arithmetic). Whether that is a miss depends on which consensus is live. Against a $177M revenue bar it is a ~4-6% miss; against the $0.21 EPS bar, which already implies about -8% non-GAAP profit QoQ, it is roughly in line. Futu shows how the market treats such a quarter: its revenue beat a consensus that had been cut to about -13% QoQ, and the stock was bid. Brokers at the lows on ~5x earnings, with a buyback in place, have been rewarded for reset numbers. The 13:00 window is likely to be dominated by the tape (QQQ swinging 5-7% a day) and by any Q4-to-date commentary on the call. November's volatility usually lifts retail volume, which helps that commentary. I see no dated evidence that tilts the release clearly either way against what the price holds. Slight lean down on the possibility that Tiger's revenue consensus was never reset the way Futu's was, partly offset by the reset-and-rally pattern Futu just showed.

recommendation.reason: The deciding lines are Q3 commissions and the Q4-to-date commentary. Futu's 2026-11-19 print already showed the market the size of the Q3 volume step-down, and TIGR moved with it that day. The only possible gap is a revenue consensus ($177M) that may not have been cut the way Futu's was, but its date and source are uncertain, and the $0.21 EPS consensus looks roughly right. With QQQ moving 5-7% a day, the tape will swamp a small edge inside a 13:00 window.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 commissions down less than 10% QoQ with net new funded accounts clearly above 32.6k, or strong Q4-to-date volume and a buyback acceleration, would make this an up print. A revenue line in the low $160Ms with negative mainland and net-asset commentary would make it a clear down print.

self_critique: The case for down: Tiger leans more on US stocks and options than Futu (its Q2 US volume rose 88% QoQ), so its commission decline could exceed Futu's 17%. If the $177M consensus is live, a 5%+ revenue miss with weaker net adds would hit a stock that just bounced 7% with the tape. The case for up: Futu's read-through showed the market rewards reset numbers, the stock is at ~5x earnings, and Q4-to-date volumes in a very volatile November are probably strong. Both cases are plausible, and the tape will likely decide the 13:00 window, so 47 is honest.
approach_notes: P6 (take the run-in apart, high-beta noise) helped most: TIGR is a FUTU shadow in a tape moving 5-7% a day, which rules out a confident call. P3 'freshest data first' pointed straight at Futu's Nov 19 print, the single most informative item. P4 was hard to apply because the consensus itself was undated and conflicting.
